title: The Counter-Surprise
logline: Lily discovers that Robin has given each friend a different birthday and dodged every one of them for eight years, so she plans a surprise party on the roof. Robin, a journalist with four guns and a startle reflex, runs a counter-surprise, Ted and Barney change sides more often than their shirts, and Marshall, who can't keep a secret from anyone, becomes the most important pigeon in the war.
coldOpen: Kids, your Aunt Robin went eight years without a single birthday. Not because she stopped aging. Because she was very, very good at not being found.

couch.line: Is this the one where Aunt Robin pulled a gun at a party?
No, Luke. That's a different party. Several different parties.

guests.name: Irma Lindqvist
guests.role: Owner of Party Depot on Ninth Avenue since 1974. Has supplied every surprise party in Hell's Kitchen and never leaked one, speaks like a Swiss diplomat, and charges eleven dollars for discretion.

guests.name: Dale
guests.role: A singing telegram in a red bellhop suit who sang one birthday greeting at Robin's news desk in 2008, and keeps trying to sing his way through her interrogation.

scenes.summary: War room at Barney's, the one place Robin never goes. Lily's grown-up birthday wall reveals Robin has given each friend a different birthday, each with an out-of-town excuse. Lily found the real one in Robin's passport: Saturday. Barney appoints himself station chief and hands out codenames; Marshall gets Sieve. Lily imagines the party; Ted is the lure. Button: Robin calls Marshall, and Marshall denies everything, specifically.

beats.line: It started, like most wars, with construction paper.
Every year I make a birthday wall for my kindergartners. This year, I made one for you guys.
Every one of you has a cupcake on this wall. Except one.
beats.title: The Grown-Up Birthday Wall
lines: Ted: April 25th. Wants a cake shaped like a building.
Marshall: Spring. Two hotdishes. Do not ask.

beats.line: Robin's birthday is in October. She's always in Vermont that week, covering the leaves. They change every year.
No, it's March. She goes to the maple syrup festival in Ottawa. She brings me back a tiny bottle.
You're both wrong. Robin's a leap-year baby. February twenty-ninth.
Technically, she's eight years old. It explains the temper.
She told me Canada abolished birthdays in 1982.
Huh. That's actually the year Canada patriated its constitution.
Ted, she knew you'd say that. That's why she picked it.
Four friends. Four birthdays. Every single one, she's out of town. Eight years, and not one cake.
Not one cake?
So how do you know the real one?
I checked her passport.
Lily!
It was in her purse, next to a handgun. I had to be fast.
May twenty-fourth. This Saturday. Surprise party, on the roof, at nine. And this time, she's coming.
Lily. You can't surprise Scherbatsky with amateurs. She reads people for a living. She owns a police scanner.
You need tradecraft. You need a station chief.
Fine. The operation is called Operation Happy Birthday Robin.
Never put the target in the name.
Operation Happy Birthday... Someone.
Chilling. I love it.
Codenames. Lily is Den Mother. I'm Daddy.
Can I be Architect?
Ted, a codename can't be your opening line at bars.
Ooh! Can I be Bigfoot?
Marshall, you're Sieve.
Sieve? Why Sieve?
Last Christmas, you told Robin what her Secret Santa gift was. Before you bought it.
I was excited about the scarf!
When Robin walks onto that roof and sees all of us, she'll finally get it.
Surprise!
Oh, Lily. You were right. About birthdays. About everything.
From now on, you plan all my birthdays. And my wedding. And my outfits.
I know, sweetie. I know.
Lily, in that version, Robin let you pick her outfits.
It's a surprise party, Ted. Anything can happen.
You're the lure. Tell her you need to talk about something serious. She always comes for your crises.
I don't have that many crises.
Ted, you had a crisis about a font last week.
Papyrus on a children's hospital is a crisis, Lily!
What about me? What's my job?
Baby, your job is to know nothing.
I can do that. I did it for my whole first year of law school!
It's Robin.
Do not answer that.
Hey, Robin! Saturday? Nope! Nothing's happening on Saturday. Definitely not on a roof.
Who said cake? Nobody said cake. Gotta go, love you, bye!
Sieve.

scenes.summary: Robin opens an investigation at the studio. Ted's lure collapses instantly; Robin lists the evidence, and Patrice outs herself as Lily's asset. Robin insists she's calm under surprises; a flashback to a 2008 singing telegram says otherwise. Robin announces a counter-surprise and turns Ted with the promise of a trench-coat arc, then feeds Marshall fake Winnipeg intel. Barney defects to her too. Button: Barney isn't on a side, he is a side.

beats.line: The next morning, your Aunt Robin did what any journalist would do. She opened an investigation.
Robin! Hey. Saturday, nine o'clock, the roof. I need to talk to you about something serious.
About what?
A cornice.
Ted. Marshall told me.
What? When?
Last night. By phone. In the form of a denial.
And then there's the rest. Lily asked my favorite frosting in a casual voice. Lily doesn't have a casual voice.
Barney called me Robin. Twice. And Patrice has been humming since Tuesday.
I always hum!
Not in a major key.
Lily says I'm an asset! Nobody's ever called me an asset before!
Nobody asked you, Patrice!
I'm baking you a cake shaped like Canada! I did Nunavut in coconut!
Okay. It's a surprise party. Robin, surprises are good for you.
Ted, I'm fine with surprises. I'm a newswoman. I'm very calm under pressure.
Kids, your Aunt Robin was a lot of things. Calm under surprises was not one of them.
Happy birthday, Robin Scherbatsky, your mother loves you so!
Get down! Hands where I can see them!
It's a singing telegram!
Who sent you?
Your mother!
My mother doesn't know where I work. Who are you really working for?
Please, I just do the songs! I have a balloon!
What happened to that guy?
He's fine. He's a mime now.
This party's happening whether I like it or not. So I'm running a counter-surprise.
I find the party first, and I surprise the surprisers. I just need a man on the inside.
A double agent?
The conflicted one. In the trench coat. He always gets the best scene in the movie.
I'm in.
That was fast.
Robin, I own four trench coats. One is for spring.
Robin! Hi! I brought you a sandwich! For no reason! It is not a birthday sandwich!
Marshall. Can you keep a secret?
No. But I'd love to try!
On Saturday, I'll be in Winnipeg, covering a curling scandal. Don't tell Lily.
Winnipeg. Curling. Lips are sealed. I have to go now for unrelated reasons!
Robin, you just used Marshall.
Marshall isn't a leak, Ted. He's a wire service with a Minnesota accent.
Scherbatsky. I hear you're running a counter-op. I'd like to defect.
Aren't you Lily's station chief?
I'm everybody's station chief.
Wait. I'm the double agent. This is my arc!
Ted, please. In seventh grade I took two Jessicas to the same dance. Neither Jessica ever knew.
So whose side are you actually on?
Ted. I'm not on a side. I am a side.

scenes.summary: Party Depot on Ninth Avenue, where Irma has kept every surprise in Hell's Kitchen. Lily orders supplies; discretion is eleven dollars. Marshall arrives with the Winnipeg intel and learns both sides are using him: he's not a sieve, he's a pigeon. Lily takes him to the stockroom for something real. Robin and Ted arrive; a smiling standoff over a beaver pinata. Lily re-turns Ted with slow motion and a choir. Barney presents his loyalties, and Irma reveals his three orders: he declined discretion.

beats.line: Every surprise party in Hell's Kitchen went through one woman, who had never leaked a secret in thirty-eight years.
Irma, I need a hundred balloons, forty party poppers, and total discretion.
Poppers are aisle two. Discretion is eleven dollars.
You charge for discretion?
You would be amazed who declines it.
My friend Robin might come in here asking questions. She's a journalist.
Ma'am, I did the streamers for Mr. Feldman's sixtieth. Planned in 1991. Thrown in 2003. He never suspected a thing.
Lily! Big news! Robin's going to Winnipeg on Saturday! There's a curling scandal!
Baby, nobody goes to Winnipeg on purpose.
She fed you that so I'd cancel the party.
She used me?
Sweetie, everyone's using you. I've been feeding you fake intel since Wednesday.
Wait. I'm not a sieve. I'm a pigeon. I'm a big, dumb carrier pigeon.
Buddy, you're the most reliable asset in this whole war. You've never once failed to deliver.
I wanted to be Bigfoot.
Marshmallow. Come to the stockroom with me. I need you for something. This one's real.
Irma, what's in the stockroom?
Private consultations. Those are free.
Free? But discretion is eleven dollars!
Discretion is a lot of work.
Barney.
Scherbatsky.
Irma.
Ma'am.
Irma, I'll give you fifty dollars to tell me where Lily's party is.
I don't take sides, ma'am. I take cash.
I'm offering you cash.
For merchandise.
Robin! What a coincidence.
Lily. Shopping for a party?
A pinata. For my class.
Shaped like what?
A beaver.
The national animal of Canada.
Kids love Canada.
Enjoy Winnipeg.
Enjoy your class.
Ted. You know what's better than a double agent? A triple agent. The one who was loyal all along.
Go on.
They reveal him at the very end. In slow motion.
Slow motion?
With a choir.
I'm yours.
Dad. You switched sides because someone said slow motion?
Penny, she said choir.
Barney. Whose side are you on?
Yes, Barney. Whose side?
Ladies. As you can see, I am loyal to the game.
beats.title: Barney's Loyalties

beats.line: Also, Mr. Stinson has placed three orders here this week. For three different parties.
Irma! What about discretion?
You declined discretion, sir. It was eleven dollars.

scenes.summary: Saturday, eight-thirty. Robin storms the roof to counter-surprise the party and finds only Lily: everyone else is at MacLaren's, because Lily knew Robin would know. Lily called Robin's mom. Robin explains: she shares a birthday with Queen Victoria, and the fireworks were never for her. Lily's gift is one forty-dollar firework from a guy in Hoboken. It's tiny; it's the best one ever. Lily undercuts: she won. The guys burst in; Robin's reflexes kick in. Marshall kept the real plan for fifty-one minutes and earns Vault. Robin's callback to Winnipeg; Future Ted's button on the firework guy.

beats.line: Saturday, eight-thirty. Your Aunt Robin went up to the roof to surprise her own surprise party.
Surprise!
Happy birthday.
Where is everyone?
MacLaren's. Guarding a cake shaped like Canada.
Ted told me the party moved to MacLaren's. Barney told me Ted was lying.
And Marshall said nothing. Nothing at all. It's the scariest thing Marshall has ever done.
I knew you'd figure out it was the roof. So I sent everybody else to the bar.
You triple-crossed me. With your own husband.
He's very reliable.
So that's it? No crowd? Nobody jumping out from behind the water tower?
Robin, I know why you skip your birthday. I called your mom.
You called my mother?
She talks a lot when somebody asks about you. I don't think anybody asks.
Then you know it's stupid.
Tell me anyway.
I was born on May twenty-fourth. So was Queen Victoria.
In Canada, that's a holiday. Every town sets off fireworks. Until I was nine, I thought they were for me.
What happened when you were nine?
My dad explained the British monarchy. Then he handed me a hunting knife and told me to walk it off.
Every year after that, the whole country threw a party on my birthday. For a dead lady in a black dress.
So I figured, if the day isn't really mine, why show up for it?
That's why there's no crowd. I didn't want to throw you one more party for somebody else.
Okay, Vince. Light it.
Who's Vince?
A guy in Hoboken with one firework. I paid him forty dollars. It's for you. I told him twice.
I don't see anything.
It's New Jersey. Give it a second.
There.
It's very small.
It was forty dollars.
It's the best one I've ever had.
Also, I won.
What?
Eight years undefeated, Scherbatsky. And you just got surprised. By one firework.
Damn it.
Surprise!
Get down! Hands where I can see them!
Robin, it's us! We brought Canada!
You're supposed to be at MacLaren's.
We were. For fifty-one minutes. Then Marshall cracked.
Fifty-one minutes! Lily, I kept a secret for fifty-one minutes!
He told Carl. Then he told the cake. Then he told us.
Baby, that's a personal record. Agent Vault.
Vault! Did you hear that? I'm Vault!
Lily, you promised me slow motion.
Ted, you came up four flights carrying a cake. That was slow motion.
Relax, Scherbatsky. I planned for every outcome. Party B is in the stairwell.
Party C is a singing telegram in the lobby. Apparently, he only does mime now.
Dale?
Same time next year?
Next year, I'll be in Winnipeg.
Kids, every May twenty-fourth since, a guy in Hoboken has lit one forty-dollar firework. He's never asked who it's for. He assumes it's for some queen.
